newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians to inaugurate Gaza airport on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians to inaugurate Gaza airport on Friday.

text.p: Palestinians will inaugurate their first airport on Friday when President Yasser Arafat's private jet flies into the self-ruled Gaza Strip, a Palestinian aviation official said on Tuesday.

"The president's jet is scheduled to arrive at the Gaza International Airport on Friday. The president will leave on Saturday and return five days later," Fayez Zaidan, head of the Civil Aviation Authority, told a news conference.
Israel, in a gesture to ease tensions over its start of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, agreed on Monday to let Arafat use the $16 million airport for his personal flights.
The arrangement does not permit commercial flights -- still a subject of Israeli-Palestinian negotiations.

Zaidan said the Palestinian airport had been ready for day flights for more than six months. Israel is demanding full security control over the airport, saying self-rule deals with the Palestinians give it overall security responsibility.

Arafat's personal jet has been based in Egypt's al-Arish airport and the Palestinian leader had to fly there by helicopter from a Gaza City pad next to his office or drive across the border each time he wanted to leave.

Zaidan insisted there was no linkage between Arafat's use of the airport and work on a 6,500-unit housing project for Jews that began on Tuesday at a disputed hill on the southern outskirts of Jerusalem.
